children.text: This moment is considered profound because of the climax of the game is a cutscene where the player is the passenger and at the whims of the game instead of the reverse. The player has no control over how this section of the narrative unfolds.

The context of the modern day has led to the writing of games like Metal Gear Solid 2, which are seen as eerily prophetic with how accurate the observations made by the writers behind the games seem, despite being made 2 decades ago.

This idea of playing on the gamers instinct to listen to the in-game authority figure/advisor, is played with throughout the series as Kojima constantly subverts their expectations by having them become unreliable guides.

The games are able to provide complex and difficult political ideas simply as they demonstrates how terrifying AI can become when it's basing its understanding purely on ideology, without being checked by any morality.

The “memes as inherited ideas” framework comes from Dawkins’ The Selfish Gene (1976). Metal Gear Solid 2 puts it in a mainstream action game, in 2001, before “meme” meant internet jokes. It’s an example of games carrying heavy ideas at a time when they were rarely expected to.

The AI's worry about information overload and people retreating into sources that confirm what they already believe. The narrator highlights just how far ahead of its time this was. It’s often cited as a reason Metal Gear Solid 2 holds up as speculative fiction rather than just a period piece.

One of the best ways to show the evolution of video game writing how the way villains have become.The villains are not cartoonish in the method of evil, but make the players question their own beliefs and consider the arguments being presented to them by the antagonists.
